correctness.rationale: The finite standard-monomial set is an order ideal containing 0, and the nonconstant span is the nilpotent maximal ideal J. The constant section splits the units as k^× times 1+J. An element with p^r-th power 1 must have constant term 1 since gcd(p,q−1)=1. Frobenius acts by the coefficient-field automorphism and injective dilation on exponent vectors until a monomial vanishes, so the kernel on J has N−s_r free coefficients, giving q^(N−s_r). In the cyclic decomposition each C_(p^a) contributes min(a,r) to K_r; differencing twice gives the claimed multiplicities, which vanish eventually because only 0 survives all dilations. This includes r=0 and the case R=k. An independent GF(4) multiplication replay in branches/audit-replays/moments_and_units.py checked the complete order histogram for (x^3,y^2,x^2y), giving C_3 × C_2^4 × C_4^2 as predicted.
residual_risks: The replay is one extension-field example, not a proof for general ideals; the monomial-basis argument supplies that proof. No classification of ring isomorphisms or nonmonomial ideals is implied.

evidence: The Frobenius-shadow theorem applies to every finite-field Artinian monomial quotient and also gives a Loewy-length counterexample family.

Chebolu et al. classify the elementary abelian unit-group case, not all cyclic exponents. Angeltveit et al. compute multi-relative K-groups using Witt vectors; those output groups are not the ordinary groups of units at issue.

It supplies no separate obstruction, family, or unit-group distinction not given by that classification.
